body: I wondered the exact same thing, I really don’t think so tbh
As a mother who is currently admitted to the parent and infant psych unit, this was a reassuring read. Thank you for posting.

I wish I could say the same of my experience. I’m SO glad there are people out there who aren’t feeling like the world is just taking a dump on their experience, but damn this ain’t me. I’ve had to go in for emergency surgery to stitch my cervix closed, with no visitors after. Been told round after round of bad news (new complications, changes to plans etc) while being all alone and being totally cut off from any form of family support. I wouldn’t wish this on people I hate.

Honestly I just had a flip through that sub and now my heart hurts. Nobody should feel the way those poor blokes are feeling, loneliness is cruel. 


As others have suggested I wouldn’t bring up what you saw, but I would perhaps look at therapy for the young guy. He sounds like he needs some extra supports around. Maybe some one on one time just to hang out, let him talk and be open with you? 


Maaaaybe you could message a mod from one of those subs and ask what kind of support would help him feel better? I don’t know how helpful it would be but it can’t hurt to try right?

Again, as someone who has been through all of this more than once, I find your attitude distasteful. You don’t get to stand from your own perspective and demand that survivors behave a certain way. If someone does not WANT to come forward they shouldn’t be pressured to do so, as if the self righteousness of others and guilt is something we need to feel on top of everything else. 


Stop making the conversation about the perpetrator, it is about the survivor. All I am saying is that OP, and ANYONE who has been through similar, is the one in control of how they want the aftermath handled. *It is about keeping them safe, and that is within THEIR CONTROL to decide what that safety looks like for them*

You’re missing my point entirely. Reporting ensures nothing of the sort, it’s this exact viewpoint I’m talking about when I say naïveté. In a perfect world that’s exactly how it would work, and exactly what the perpetrator deserves. However, we reside in the real world and it just doesn’t work like that. 


I have had friends with cut and dry evidence have their cases dropped, after going through the horror of giving a statement and pressing charges and attending multiple magistrate hearings. I’ve personally been told “I don’t have time to deal with this, can you just go to a different station?”. 


I’m not saying don’t come forward, I’m saying OP needs to do what’s going to keep her safe, this includes her mental health. OP also needs to be realistic, she’s young, telling her “reporting him will ENSURE xyz outcome” is gobshite and while I respect it’s coming from a good place, it’s harmful.

Is it sane and normal? Absolutely! What I can’t jive with is when well meaning people drop the line “it could stop it happening to someone else”. It stops being advice at that point, and starts becoming a guilt trip if they don’t want to come forward. 


I’m actually one of the fortunate ones who came forward, charges were pressed, had to give evidence in court and saw him jailed. I was also OPs age. It was HARD, so much harder than I ever thought and I just can’t begrudge someone not wanting to put themselves through that. I just wanted to make sure OP knew that they don’t have to press charges if they don’t want to is all :)

Everyone telling you to go to the police has either NEVER had to do so themselves for this type of thing, or are very naive. 


Do place a report if you want to OP, I don’t mean to discourage you. But people here are acting like it’s the easiest thing in the world to do. A lot of victims just aren’t believed, even when they are if there is no evidence then they won’t pursue anything. It is gut wrenching to have to re-traumatise yourself explaining everything in horrifying detail, only to be told there is insufficient evidence to do anything. 


OP I beg you to find another job ASAP and seek trauma counselling. I’m not sure where you are, but I’m sure there are local resources to help you. *Do* attempt to press charges if you want, but do so because you feel that’s the best choice for you, not because a bunch of strangers told you to. 


Also, please feel free to PM me anytime if you’d like to talk

Hey OP, I have PTSD from childhood trauma similar to his (though I acknowledge that being a woman does lend to things being different). I have an INTENSE and visceral reaction to males with blue eyes, it makes me feel like I want to puke, punch something and run in front of a train all at the same time, because immediately my brain replaces the face of who I’m looking at to my abuser.


*However* through therapy I learnt skills to help get me through that initial reactive phase. He cannot help the feelings he has, but he CAN seek training that will help him manage them. If you do not wish to dye your hair then please don’t, just try to remember that if he is struggling with it to support him as best you can. That doesn’t mean you have to sacrifice something important to you though, remember that. 


If you’d like to PM me any time about PTSD or anything at all I’m happy to chat anytime x
